scope: Offline Swara MVP survival guidance for medical, fire, flood, earthquake, violence or personal safety, lost, and general emergencies. School-shooting and active-shooter guidance are excluded from this pack.

packs.title: Medical Emergency Pack
packs.sourceLabel: Red Cross, Stop the Bleed, Mayo Clinic
quickHelp: Check scene safety before touching the person.
For heavy bleeding, apply firm direct pressure with clean cloth or gauze.
If bleeding soaks through, add more cloth and keep pressing.
Call local emergency help if reachable, especially for severe bleeding, trouble breathing, chest pain, or unconsciousness.
detailedSteps: Move yourself and the injured person away from immediate danger if it is safe.
Check responsiveness and breathing. If the person is not breathing normally, emergency help is urgent.
For severe bleeding, expose the wound enough to see it, then press firmly and continuously.
Keep the person still, warm, and lying down if they feel faint or weak.
Do not remove embedded objects. Press around the object and stabilize it.
Do not give food or drink to a person who may need urgent medical care.
doNot: Do not use a tourniquet unless bleeding is life-threatening and direct pressure is not enough or impossible.
Do not remove deep embedded objects.
Do not delay pressure on severe bleeding while searching for perfect supplies.

packs.title: Fire Emergency Pack
quickHelp: Leave the building immediately if there is fire, smoke, or alarm.
Stay low under smoke and cover nose and mouth if needed.
Feel doors before opening. If hot, use another exit.
Once outside, stay out and call emergency help if reachable.
detailedSteps: Alert people nearby while moving toward the safest exit.
If smoke is present, crawl or stay low because cleaner air is usually lower.
Before opening a closed door, check heat with the back of your hand.
Close doors behind you if possible to slow fire spread.
Go to a safe meeting point away from the structure.
If trapped, seal gaps around doors, signal from a window, and call for help if possible.
doNot: Do not re-enter a burning or smoky building.
Do not use elevators during a fire.
Do not hide in closets or bathrooms if evacuation is possible.
kit: N95 or cloth face covering if available

packs.title: Flood Emergency Pack
quickHelp: Move to higher ground immediately if water is rising.
Avoid walking, swimming, or driving through floodwater.
Stay away from downed power lines and electrical equipment in wet areas.
Use safe bottled, boiled, or treated water if normal water may be contaminated.
detailedSteps: If evacuation is ordered or water is rising, leave early by a safe route.
Move important medicines, documents, and phone charging supplies into a waterproof bag if time allows.
Avoid bridges or roads covered by water because the road surface may be damaged or missing.
If trapped in a building, move to a higher floor, but avoid closed attics without roof escape.
After flooding, avoid contact with floodwater when possible because it may contain sewage, chemicals, or debris.
If wet electrical equipment or outlets are present, stay away until power is confirmed off.
doNot: Do not drive through floodwater.
Do not touch electrical devices while standing in water.
Do not drink untreated flood-contaminated water.

packs.title: Earthquake Emergency Pack
quickHelp: During shaking, drop, cover, and hold on.
Stay away from glass, windows, heavy furniture, and falling objects.
If outside, move to an open area away from buildings, trees, and power lines.
After shaking stops, check injuries, fire, gas smell, unstable structures, and safe exit routes.
detailedSteps: Drop to hands and knees so the shaking does not knock you down.
Cover head and neck under sturdy furniture if available, or beside an interior wall away from glass.
Hold on to shelter until shaking stops.
If in bed, stay there and protect your head with a pillow unless a heavy object may fall on you.
After shaking, expect aftershocks and move carefully around broken glass or debris.
If you smell gas, hear hissing, or see fire risk, leave the area and avoid flames or switches.
doNot: Do not run outside during active shaking if you are indoors.
Do not stand in doorways unless it is the only nearby sturdy cover.
Do not use elevators after an earthquake.

packs.title: Violence and Personal Safety Pack
packs.sourceLabel: Ready.gov public spaces, NIH workplace violence prevention
quickHelp: Move away from the threat if there is a clear safe path.
Create distance, get behind a barrier, and avoid confrontation if possible.
Call local emergency help or a trusted contact when it is safe to do so.
If you are with others, move together toward a safer public or staffed area.
detailedSteps: Trust immediate warning signs such as threats, stalking, escalating anger, weapon display, or blocked exits.
Leave early if you can do so without escalating the situation.
Keep your voice low, use short words, and avoid arguing if de-escalation is the safest option.
Move toward lighted, public, staffed, or populated areas when possible.
Share your location and situation with a trusted person when it is safe.
After reaching safety, document key details such as time, place, description, injuries, witnesses, and messages.
doNot: Do not argue, threaten, film openly, or challenge the person if it increases danger.
Do not stay to collect belongings if leaving is the safer option.
Do not return alone to a place where the threat may still be present.
Do not treat this pack as school-shooting or active-shooter guidance.
kit: Whistle or personal alarm if available

packs.title: Lost or Stranded Pack
packs.sourceLabel: US Forest Service, National Park Service
quickHelp: Stop moving unless staying put is immediately dangerous.
Stay visible and make signals with sound, light, color, or movement.
Conserve phone battery and send your location if signal exists.
Prepare shelter before dark or bad weather.
detailedSteps: Stop, breathe, and avoid panic movement that makes search harder.
Check for immediate hazards such as cold, heat, injury, rising water, or unstable ground.
If you have signal, contact help and share location, landmarks, direction of travel, and condition.
Mark your location with bright objects, ground markings, or repeated signals.
Use a whistle, mirror, flashlight, or three repeated signals to attract attention.
Protect warmth and dryness before night; use layers, natural windbreaks, and insulation from the ground.
Drink safe water if available, but avoid unknown plants or unsafe water treatment claims.
doNot: Do not wander randomly after realizing you are lost.
Do not split from your group.
Do not drain your phone with nonessential use.

packs.title: General Emergency Pack
quickHelp: Move away from immediate danger if it is safe.
Check breathing, severe bleeding, fire, floodwater, unstable structures, and unsafe electricity.
Contact local emergency help if reachable.
Use one clear next action instead of doing many things at once.
detailedSteps: Identify the most immediate threat to life: breathing, severe bleeding, fire, water, collapse, exposure, or violence nearby.
Move to a safer place only if movement reduces risk.
Stabilize urgent medical risks first, especially severe bleeding or abnormal breathing.
Preserve phone battery and send location to a trusted contact if possible.
Gather essential items only if it does not delay escape: water, medicine, documents, light, and phone power.
Ask one critical question at a time to decide the next safest step.
doNot: Do not delay evacuation to collect nonessential items.
Do not enter unsafe structures, floodwater, smoke, or unstable areas.
Do not give instructions beyond the known situation.
